classification.difficultyReason: Work backwards through two fractional spending stages with fixed monetary adjustments.

content.prompt: Jessica was preparing for her birthday party. She spent $\$3$ less than $\frac{3}{5}$ of her money on soft drink and $\$3$ more than $\frac{3}{4}$ of her remaining money on food. She still had $\$3$ left. How much did she start with?

answer.short:
$\$52.50$

Work backwards, undoing each fixed adjustment before reconstructing the whole from the remaining fraction.
answer.worked:
After buying food, the extra $\$3$ spent leaves $\$3$, so one-quarter of the money available before buying food was $\$6$.
$$\begin{align*}\text{Money before buying food}&=(3+3)\times4\\\text{Money before buying food}&=24\end{align*}$$
Spending $\$3$ less than three-fifths leaves two-fifths of the original money plus $\$3$.
$$\begin{align*}\text{Two-fifths of the original money}&=24-3\\\text{Two-fifths of the original money}&=21\\\text{Original money}&=21\div2\times5\\\text{Original money}&=52.50\end{align*}$$
Jessica started with $\$52.50$.

Check: soft drink cost $\frac35\times\$52.50-\$3=\$28.50$, leaving $\$24$. Food cost $\frac34\times\$24+\$3=\$21$, leaving $\$3$.
